title: きっと — “surely / certainly”
summary: きっと is an adverb that shows the speaker's strong conviction that something will happen or is so. It usually goes with ～だろう, ～でしょう, ～と思う or a plain statement about the future.

patterns.form: きっと ＋ 文（〜だろう／〜でしょう／〜と思う）
patterns.gloss: きっと来るだろう (He will surely come)

patterns.form: きっと ＋ 動詞（する・なる）
patterns.gloss: In a promise or encouragement, it can be followed by a plain verb: きっと上手になる

body.p: As an adverb it never changes form. Placed in a sentence, it marks what follows as almost certain. Often there is a reason behind it, as in 約束したから、きっと来る.
Use it for predictions about the future (彼女はきっと成功する), encouragement (毎日練習すれば、きっと上手になる) and promises. With だろう it becomes softer: confident but not flatly asserting.
It is more confident than かもしれない and differs from 必ず. 必ず expresses that a person's will or promise will certainly be kept (必ず行きます); きっと is a prediction or conviction, not a guarantee.

examples.ja: 彼女（かのじょ）はきっと成功（せいこう）します。
約束（やくそく）したから、彼（かれ）はきっと来（く）るだろう。
examples.romaji: Yakusoku shita kara, kare wa kitto kuru darō.
examples.tr: He promised, so he'll surely come.

examples.ja: 毎日（まいにち）練習（れんしゅう）すれば、きっと上手（じょうず）になる。
examples.romaji: Mainichi renshū sureba, kitto jōzu ni naru.
examples.tr: If you practice every day, you'll surely get better.

pitfalls: For a firm promise about your own will, use 必ず. きっと行きます is closer to “I think I'll go” and is weak as a promise.
It is awkward for stating past facts; use a guessing form such as きっと～だっただろう.
